zh.title: 美國挪用瑞士F-35購機款支付愛國者飛彈瑞士削減訂單考慮歐洲戰機
zh.summary: 美國2025年暫停向瑞士交付愛國者飛彈後，動用瑞士F-35戰機採購帳戶逾1億瑞士法郎支付飛彈款項；瑞士將F-35訂單由36架減至30架，國防部長4月宣布正談判終止整份愛國者飛彈合約，聯邦委員會則評估以歐洲戰機搭配F-35組成混合機隊。
body: 2025年，美國告知瑞士領導人將暫停交付雷神愛國者飛彈，理由是供應鏈須優先向烏克蘭供貨並補充美國本土庫存。瑞士政府隨即停止支付資助愛國者飛彈計畫的外國軍事銷售合約款項，但美方直接從瑞士戰機採購專款中扣除了未付餘額；根據美瑞外國軍事銷售協議條款，華府有權在某一計畫資金短缺時調動瑞士任何國防計畫的資金池，美方因此依法轉移了逾1億瑞士法郎、約1.26億美元。
瑞士正將機隊由波音F/A-18大黃蜂過渡至洛克希德·馬丁F-35A閃電II式戰機，2021年已預付訂金以確保生產線位置。美方不僅要求瑞士償還被挪用的飛彈款項，還以生產成本上漲、通膨與供應鏈壓力為由，主張合約原始固定價格無法執行，要求追加7.6億至15億美元；瑞士拒絕支付更高費用，將訂單削減兩成，由36架減至30架。

瑞士軍備局長烏爾斯·洛赫形容情況「非常不令人滿意」。今年4月，瑞士國防部長馬丁·普菲斯特宣布，瑞士正積極談判可能終止整份愛國者飛彈合約；6月，瑞士聯邦院批准追加5.05億美元信貸。首架瑞士F-35A已在洛克希德·馬丁喬治亞州瑪麗埃塔廠進入主要組裝階段，但美國政府問責局報告證實，早期交付的瑞士戰機將採用簡化的Block 4軟體配置，完整Block 4現代化最早要到2031年才能就緒；首批飛機將部署於阿肯色州埃賓空軍國民警衛隊基地進行飛行員訓練，實體運抵瑞士的時間延至2028年。瑞士聯邦委員會已表示，未來若要將機隊恢復至原本需要的36架，將獨立評估機型，不限於F-35，正在考慮以30架F-35搭配歐洲製4.5代戰機組成混合機隊，候選機型包括颱風、飆風與獅鷲戰機。

en.title: US tapped Switzerland's F-35 funds to pay for Patriot missiles — what happened next
en.summary: The United States paused Patriot missile deliveries to Switzerland in 2025, then withdrew more than 100 million Swiss francs from funds earmarked for Swiss F-35 fighters to cover the bill; Switzerland cut its F-35 order from 36 to 30 jets, and Bern is now weighing European fighters to pair with the F-35s.
body: The crunch on America's strategic missile stockpile put Switzerland in a tough position in 2025, when the United States informed Swiss leaders that it would pause Raytheon Patriot missile deliveries. Washington said the supply chain diversion was necessary to prioritize shipments to Ukraine and replenish the domestic arsenal. The Swiss government halted payments under its foreign military sales contract funding the Patriot program, but the US simply withdrew the outstanding balance from cash earmarked for Swiss fighters: under the FMS agreements, Washington had the authority to take funding from any pool of Swiss defense program funds, and redirected well over 100 million Swiss francs, or $126 million.

Switzerland is transitioning its fleet from the Boeing F/A-18 Hornet to the Lockheed Martin F-35A Lightning II, and had paid up front in 2021 to secure its position on the production line. American officials not only demanded that the Swiss repay the funds withdrawn for Patriot missiles, but also increased the total based on rising production costs, inflation and supply chain pressures, claiming the contract's original fixed price could not be enforced and demanding an additional $760 million to $1.5 billion. Instead of paying higher fees, Switzerland cut its order by 20 percent, dropping from 36 Joint Strike Fighters to 30.

Urs Loher, head of the Swiss Armaments Agency Armasuisse, described the situation as "very unsatisfactory," and was quoted as saying that "the risk was too great for us. We'll take whatever we can get." In April, Swiss Defense Minister Martin Pfister announced that Switzerland is actively negotiating a potential termination of the entire Patriot missile contract, and in June 2026 the Swiss Council of States approved an additional credit of $505 million. The first Swiss F-35A has entered main assembly at Lockheed Martin's Marietta, Georgia, plant, but a US Government Accountability Office report confirmed that the early Swiss aircraft will be delivered in a truncated Block 4 software configuration, with full Block 4 modernization not ready until 2031 at the earliest; the initial aircraft will be deployed to Ebbing Air National Guard Base in Arkansas for pilot training, with physical arrivals in Switzerland delayed until 2028. The Swiss Federal Council has said any future purchases to restore the fleet to 36 aircraft will be evaluated independently of aircraft type, and Switzerland is considering pairing the 30 F-35s with 4.5-generation European-made aircraft, with the Eurofighter, Rafale and Gripen the leading contenders.

facts.claim: In 2025 the United States informed Swiss leaders that it would pause Raytheon Patriot missile deliveries, saying the supply chain diversion was necessary to prioritize shipments to Ukraine and replenish the domestic arsenal.

Under the FMS agreements between the US and Switzerland, Washington had the authority to take funding from any pool of Swiss defense program funds, and it redirected well over 100 million Swiss francs, or $126 million.

Switzerland had paid up front in 2021 to secure its position on the F-35 production line, and the US is demanding an additional $760 million to $1.5 billion, claiming the contract's original fixed price could not be enforced.
Instead of paying higher fees, Switzerland cut its order by 20 percent, dropping from 36 Joint Strike Fighters to 30.

In April, Swiss Defense Minister Martin Pfister announced that Switzerland is actively negotiating a potential termination of the entire Patriot missile contract, and in June 2026 the Swiss Council of States approved an additional credit of $505 million.

A US Government Accountability Office report confirmed that the early Swiss aircraft will be delivered in a truncated Block 4 software configuration, with full Block 4 modernization not ready until 2031 at the earliest, and physical arrivals in Switzerland delayed until 2028.

The Swiss Federal Council stated that any future purchases to bring the fleet back up to 36 aircraft will be evaluated independently of aircraft type, and Switzerland is considering pairing the 30 F-35s with 4.5-generation European-made aircraft.
